guarantees.claim: A fixed-priority arbiter instance u_appid_arb is instantiated with N=NumAppIntf, DW=1, EnDataPort=0, connecting app_reqs to req_i, arb_ready to ready_i, and driving arb_idx from idx_o, arb_valid from valid_o, unused_app_gnts from gnt_o.
With EnDataPort=0, data_i is tied to 0 and data_o is left unconnected, so the arbiter transfers no data payload.

assumptions.claim: app_reqs inputs must be stable and valid when arb_ready is low and must remain asserted until granted; otherwise grants may be missed or spurious.
Parameter NumAppIntf must be ≥ 1; a value of 0 may cause invalid instantiation or X-generation.
assumptions.risk: arbiter may be functionally broken or produce undefined outputs.

assumptions.claim: The consumer must assert arb_ready when it accepts a valid grant, otherwise the arbiter will stall and no new requests will be served.
assumptions.risk: blockage of all subsequent app request processing.

uncertain_points.claim: unused_app_gnts is driven by the arbiter but the name suggests it is unused; if truly unused, it is dead logic.
uncertain_points.risk: unnecessary resource usage; potential design oversight.

uncertain_points.claim: If arb_ready is stuck low, the arbiter will never grant, blocking all app request processing.
uncertain_points.risk: permanent denial of service for app interface arbitration.

uncertain_points.claim: Parameter NumAppIntf is used without a guard for zero; if set to zero, the instantiation may be invalid.
arb_idx is used externally to index into an array or memory; if the consumer does not bound-check, an out-of-range request could yield invalid access.
uncertain_points.risk: memory corruption or array index overflow.
